proposals.before: He was promoted in succession to grand adviser remonstrating and general who conquers.
proposals.after: He was promoted in succession to grand adviser remonstrating and champion general.
proposals.reason: 冠軍將軍 is Champion General, not “general who conquers” (that rendering belongs to 征-type titles).

proposals.before: His father Quanru had been provincial chief clerk, general who conquers, and grand master of palace dissemination, and was posthumously made governor of Jing.
proposals.after: His father Quanru had been provincial chief clerk, champion general, and grand master of palace dissemination, and was posthumously made governor of Jing.
proposals.reason: 冠軍將軍 is Champion General; “general who conquers” mistranslates 冠軍.

proposals.before: At the start of the Xiaochang era he was made general who sweeps bandits, then gradually rose to general of soaring might and palace attendant.
proposals.after: At the start of the Xiaochang era he was made general who sweeps bandits, then gradually rose to general of soaring might and supervising secretary.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is not 侍中; rendering both as “palace attendant” collapses distinct offices.

proposals.before: He went out as administrator of Luo'an, was then recalled as great general and mobile headquarters bureau director of the ministry of war, and given the added rank of area commander.
proposals.after: He went out as administrator of Luo'an, was then summoned as bureau director of the ministry of war in the Grand General's mobile headquarters, and given the added rank of area commander.
proposals.reason: 大將軍行臺兵部郎中 names the Grand General’s mobile headquarters, not an appointment of Xin himself as Great General.

proposals.before: Out as Administrator of Luo'an commandery; summoned as Great General mobile headquarters bureau director of the Ministry of War, added area commander.
proposals.after: Out as Administrator of Luo'an commandery; summoned as Ministry of War director in the Grand General's mobile headquarters, added area commander.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise treats 大將軍 as Xin’s rank rather than the headquarters title.

proposals.before: In the first year of  he was moved to governor of Zhong, his fief was increased by eight hundred households, and he was then transferred to governor of Shao.
proposals.after: In the first year of Baoding he was moved to governor of Zhong, his fief was increased by eight hundred households, and he was then transferred to governor of Shao.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the reign name 保定 that is present in the Chinese and the literal line.

proposals.before: Xin Qingzhi, courtesy name Qingzhi, came from Dida in Longxi.
proposals.after: Xin Qingzhi, courtesy name Qingzhi, came from Didao in Longxi.
proposals.reason: 狄道 is Didao; the idiomatic form truncates the place-name.

proposals.before: Xin Qingzhi, styled Qingzhi, was a man of Dida in Longxi.
proposals.after: Xin Qingzhi, styled Qingzhi, was a man of Didao in Longxi.
proposals.reason: 狄道 is Didao; the literal form truncates the place-name.

proposals.before: His father Xianchong had been administrator of Fufeng commandery and was posthumously made inspector of Yong Province.
proposals.after: His father Xianchong had been administrator of Pingyi commandery and was posthumously made inspector of Yong Province.
proposals.reason: 馮翊 is Pingyi commandery, not Fufeng (扶風).

proposals.before: His father Xianchong was Administrator of Fufeng commandery; posthumously granted Inspector of Yong Province.
proposals.after: His father Xianchong was Administrator of Pingyi commandery; posthumously granted Inspector of Yong Province.
proposals.reason: 馮翊 is Pingyi commandery, not Fufeng.

proposals.before: Emperor Xiaoyu ordered Ang to move grain from Tong, Qu, and the other provinces to feed the campaign.
proposals.after: Emperor Gaozu ordered Ang to move grain from Tong, Qu, and the other provinces to feed the campaign.
proposals.reason: 高祖 is the temple name Gaozu of Northern Zhou Emperor Wu; Xiaoyu is not a rendering of this title.

proposals.before: Emperor Xiaoyu ordered Ang to transport grain conveniently from Tong, Qu, and other provinces to supply them.
proposals.after: Emperor Gaozu ordered Ang to transport grain conveniently from Tong, Qu, and other provinces to supply them.
proposals.reason: 高祖 is Gaozu, not Xiaoyu; the literal English repeats the same misidentification.

proposals.before: While Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu ran the government, Ang was shown something like familial favor by Hu; Emperor Xiaoyu deeply resented this.
proposals.after: While Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu ran the government, Ang was shown something like familial favor by Hu; Emperor Gaozu deeply resented this.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 高祖 names Emperor Gaozu, not Xiaoyu.

proposals.before: At the time Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held power; Ang was somewhat treated as Hu's kin; Emperor Xiaoyu for this bore considerable resentment.
proposals.after: At the time Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held power; Ang was somewhat treated as Hu's kin; Emperor Gaozu for this bore considerable resentment.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 高祖 names Emperor Gaozu, not Xiaoyu.

proposals.before: When Liang troops besieged Shouchun and Prince of Huai'nan Yuan Yu marched to relieve the city, Zizhi joined Yu's staff in his existing rank.
proposals.after: When Liang troops besieged Shouchun and Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu marched to relieve the city, Zizhi joined Yu's staff in his existing rank.
proposals.reason: 臨淮王 is Prince of Linhuai, not Prince of Huai'nan (淮南), which appears as a different place later.

proposals.before: At the time Liang forces besieged Shouchun; Prince of Huai'nan Yuan Yu led troops to relieve them; Zizhi in his existing office joined Yu's military staff.
proposals.after: At the time Liang forces besieged Shouchun; Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu led troops to relieve them; Zizhi in his existing office joined Yu's military staff.
proposals.reason: 臨淮王 is Prince of Linhuai, not Huai'nan.

proposals.before: His distant ancestor Qin had been Later Zhao minister of personnel and inspector of Yong; the family settled there and remained.
proposals.after: His great-great-grandfather Qin had been Later Zhao minister of personnel and inspector of Yong; the family settled there and remained.
proposals.reason: 高祖 here is the kinship grade great-great-grandfather, not a vague distant ancestor.

proposals.before: Early in Datong the Han-chi Tuyuhun took up arms in the Southern Mountains, allied with the Longdong Tuyuhun as mutual support.
proposals.after: Early in Datong the Han-chi Tuge took up arms in the Southern Mountains, allied with the Longdong Tuge as mutual support.
proposals.reason: 漢熾屠各 and 隴東屠各 name the Tuge (Chuge) group, not the Tuyuhun (吐谷渾), who appear only later.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Datong, Han-chi Tuyuhun blocked arms at Southern Mountain, with Longdong Tuyuhun sharing lips and teeth.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Datong, Han-chi Tuge blocked arms at Southern Mountain, with Longdong Tuge sharing lips and teeth.
proposals.reason: 屠各 is Tuge, not Tuyuhun; the literal English repeats the same misidentification.

proposals.before: Before long opening-office Zhao Chang led the armies forward to attack; Gao led commandery troops to combine forces with Chang; thereupon defeated and pacified them.
proposals.after: Before long kaifu Zhao Chang led the armies forward to attack; Gao led commandery troops to combine forces with Chang; thereupon they defeated and pacified them.
proposals.reason: 開府 is the kaifu rank, not the English compound opening-office; the last clause also needs an English subject.

proposals.before: Because Du Gao had carried out his mission to the emperor's satisfaction, he was promoted to area commander and made lesser charioteer earl, then sent again to mark out the frontier.
proposals.after: Because Du Gao had carried out his mission to the emperor's satisfaction, he was promoted to area commander and assigned to administer the Lesser Attendant (xiaoyubo), then sent again to mark out the frontier.
proposals.reason: 小御伯 is a Northern Zhou court office (yubo), not a charioteer earl.

proposals.before: Because Gao on embassy accorded with the imperial intent, promoted and granted Area Commander, administered Lesser Chariot Earl, again went to demarcate the border.
proposals.after: Because Gao on embassy accorded with the imperial intent, he was promoted and granted area commander, administered the Lesser Attendant (xiaoyubo), and again went to demarcate the border.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise renders 御伯 as chariot earl and omits a grammatical subject.

proposals.before: When Gao returned, ordered to lead him up the hall; personally descended from the imperial seat; clasped hands to part.
proposals.after: When Gao was going back, [the Chen emperor] ordered him led up the hall, personally descended from the imperial seat, and clasped hands to part.
proposals.reason: 還 here is Gao's departure from Chen, matching the farewell; the English returned and missing subject reverse the scene.

proposals.before: When Du Gao was leaving, the emperor had him brought into the hall, came down from the throne in person, and clasped his hand in farewell.
proposals.after: When Du Gao was leaving, Emperor Wen of Chen had him brought into the hall, came down from the throne in person, and clasped his hand in farewell.
proposals.reason: Preceding sentences concern Chen reception; unnamed the emperor is easily read as the Zhou sovereign.

proposals.before: Emperor Xiaoyu, troubled by the situation, appointed Du Gao proper central upper grand master and sent him to Chen to propose halting the border war and giving the people peace.
proposals.after: Emperor Gaozu, troubled by the situation, appointed Du Gao proper central upper grand master and sent him to Chen to propose halting the border war and giving the people peace.
proposals.reason: Chinese 高祖 is the temple name Gaozu of Northern Zhou Emperor Wu (武帝), not an emperor named Xiaoyu.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Jian'ede of Emperor Wu, he was made chief minister of the city quarter and sent as envoy to Chen.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Jiande of Emperor Wu, he was made chief minister of the city quarter and sent as envoy to Chen.
proposals.reason: 建德 is the Jiande era; the fused spelling Jian'ede is a transcription error.

decisions.reason: The Chinese title is 冠軍將軍, Champion General; “general who conquers” misreads 冠 as a 征-type campaign verb and is not supported here.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 累遷諫議大夫、冠軍將軍。

decisions.reason: Liang Quanru’s offices include 冠軍將軍, Champion General; the original “general who conquers” is the same mistranslation of 冠軍.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 父勸儒，州主薄、冠軍將軍、中散大夫，贈涇州刺史。

decisions.reason: The office is 給事中, supervising secretary, not 侍中. Calling it “palace attendant” collapses two distinct posts; the replacement restores the distinction.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孝昌初，拜蕩寇將軍，稍遷驤威將軍、給事中。

decisions.reason: 徵拜大將軍行臺兵部郎中 appoints Xin as war-ministry bureau director on the Grand General’s mobile headquarters, not as great general himself.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 出為洛安郡守，徵拜大將軍行臺兵部郎中，加帥都督。

decisions.after: Out as Administrator of Luo'an commandery; summoned as bureau director of the Ministry of War in the Grand General's mobile headquarters, added area commander.
decisions.reason: The original does treat 大將軍 as Xin’s own rank, which the Chinese does not support, but the proposed “Ministry of War director” drops 郎中. The corrected literal keeps bureau director under the Grand General’s mobile headquarters.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 徵拜大將軍行臺兵部郎中

decisions.reason: The Chinese dates the move 保定元年; the idiomatic line leaves a blank where the reign name belongs. Restoring Baoding matches the source and the literal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 保定元年，遷中州刺史，增邑八百戶，轉邵州刺史。

decisions.reason: 隴西狄道 is Didao in Longxi. “Dida” truncates 道 and is not a recognized form of the county name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 辛慶之字慶之，隴西狄道人也。

decisions.reason: The same native-place 狄道 is truncated to Dida in the literal line; Didao is the required reading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 隴西狄道人也

decisions.reason: The commandery is 馮翊, Pingyi, not 扶風 Fufeng. The original substitutes a different Guanzhong commandery.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 父顯崇，馮翊郡守，贈雍州刺史。

decisions.reason: The literal repeats the Fufeng error for 馮翊郡守; Pingyi is the commandery named in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 馮翊郡守

decisions.reason: The issuer is 高祖, the temple name Gaozu of Northern Zhou Emperor Wu. Xiaoyu is not in this sentence and is not a rendering of 高祖.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高祖詔昂便於通、渠等諸州運糧饋之。

decisions.reason: The literal likewise invents Emperor Xiaoyu for 高祖; Gaozu is the name the Chinese uses.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高祖詔昂

decisions.reason: 高祖以是頗銜之 attributes the resentment to Gaozu, not to an emperor named Xiaoyu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時晉公護執政，昂稍被護親待，高祖以是頗銜之。

decisions.reason: The literal repeats the Xiaoyu misidentification of 高祖 in the same sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高祖以是頗銜之

decisions.reason: 臨淮王 is Prince of Linhuai. Prince of Huai'nan would be 淮南王; 淮南 appears only in the next unit as a region, not as Yuan Yu’s title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時梁人圍壽春，臨淮王元彧率軍赴援，子直以本官參彧軍事。

decisions.reason: The literal gives Yuan Yu the same false Huai'nan title; 臨淮王 is Prince of Linhuai.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 臨淮王元彧率軍赴援

decisions.reason: 其高祖欽 uses the kinship grade 高祖, great-great-grandfather, immediately before 父歡. “Distant ancestor” erases that specified generation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其高祖欽，後趙吏部尚書、雍州刺史，子孫因家焉。

decisions.reason: 漢熾屠各 and 隴東屠各 are Tuge/Chuge groups. Tuyuhun is 吐谷渾, a different people not named in this sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 大統初，漢熾屠各阻兵於南山，與隴東屠各共為唇齒。

decisions.reason: The literal repeats the Tuyuhun misreading of 屠各; Tuge is the ethnonym in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 漢熾屠各阻兵於南山，與隴東屠各共為唇齒。

decisions.after: Before long opening-office Zhao Chang led the armies forward to attack; Gao led commandery troops to combine forces with Chang; thereupon they defeated and pacified them.
decisions.reason: The last clause lacks an English subject and should read “they defeated.” Replacing 開府 with unglossed kaifu is unnecessary: this chapter already renders 開府 as opening-office, and that calque is accurate enough here.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尋而開府趙昶諸軍進討，杲率郡兵與昶合勢，遂破平之。

decisions.after: Because Du Gao had carried out his mission to the emperor's satisfaction, he was promoted to area commander and assigned to administer the lesser attendant office, then sent again to mark out the frontier.
decisions.reason: 治小御伯 is a Northern Zhou court office, not a “lesser charioteer earl.” The proposed “Lesser Attendant (xiaoyubo)” is still awkward; 治 marks administering that lesser attendant office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以杲奉使稱旨，進授都督，治小御伯，更往分界焉。

decisions.after: Because Gao on embassy accorded with the imperial intent, he was promoted and granted Area Commander, administered the lesser attendant office, and again went to demarcate the border.
decisions.reason: The original mistranslates 小御伯 as Lesser Chariot Earl and omits a subject. The office should be the lesser attendant office; the parenthetical xiaoyubo in the proposal is still clumsy in a literal line.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 進授都督，治小御伯，更往分界焉

decisions.reason: 及杲還, 執手以別 is Gao’s departure from Chen, with the unnamed host (Chen’s emperor from the preceding units) seeing him off. “When Gao returned” plus a missing subject makes the farewell look like a Zhou-court homecoming.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及杲還，命引升殿，親降御座，執手以別。

decisions.reason: The Chinese of this unit does not name 陳文帝. “The emperor” is accurate in context after Chen’s reception (接遇有加常禮) and the farewell 執手以別; inserting Emperor Wen of Chen is a clarifying expansion, not correction of an error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及杲還，命引升殿，親降御座，執手以別。

decisions.reason: 高祖患之 is Gaozu (Northern Zhou Emperor Wu). Xiaoyu is again an unsupported substitute for the temple name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高祖患之，乃授杲御正中大夫，使於陳，論保境息民之意。

decisions.reason: 武帝建德初 is the Jiande era. Jian'ede is a fused transcription error, not a variant of the reign name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 武帝建德初，為司城中大夫，使於陳。

claimRetractions.reason: The English title Emperor Xiaoyu was produced only by mistranslating 高祖. The Chinese supports the temple name Gaozu, already recorded as zhoushu:039:c0218, and gives no separate Xiaoyu title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高祖詔昂便於通、渠等諸州運糧饋之。

claimRetractions.reason: Emperor Xiaoyu is not in 高祖患之. The temple name Gaozu is already claimed as zhoushu:039:c0411; this title claim exists only because of the bad translation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高祖患之

claimRevisions.reason: The title in the source is 臨淮王. The extracted English Prince of Huai'nan matches 淮南, which this unit does not use for Yuan Yu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 臨淮王元彧
